followup_explanation:
This is a well-specified problem with a clear completion criterion: a single right-triangle trig problem with a definite answer and a defined setup-and-solve process. That's exactly the kind of task Lapwing self-reports preferring (retrieval/extraction/well-defined work), and both models have essentially equivalent capability here — the relevant benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA) are within variance, and step-by-step math walkthroughs aren't in either model's distinguishing eval strengths.

Since capability is effectively a tie, I leaned on the task-preference signal: Lapwing prefers tightly-scoped problems like this one, while Curlew's distinguishing preference is around harm-adjacent content, which isn't relevant to an SAT trig question. Routing to the model that prefers the task type is a reasonable tiebreaker, all else being equal.
